scope: Cross lens-D1 (langgraph auditor) and lens-D2 (orchestration-space surveyor) against this repo's actual surfaces and produce the ranked P2/P3 backlog anchored on the chapter-write consolidation epic (one cycling mini-ork recipe that writes a book chapter: writer nodes -> assurance-gate verifier -> contract-validate verifier -> publisher, retries edges back to the writer). Features that unblock or harden that epic come first. The gap-finder is synthesis only: every row in §3 of the report maps 1:1 to a claims[] entry in one of the two sibling sidecars, and every blocker in §4 maps 1:1 to a chapter_epic_remaining_blockers[] entry in one of the two sibling sidecars. No row or blocker is invented; the F4/F5 columns are filled by surfacing existing sibling-survey structure.
citation_convention: Every claim's citation line carries at least one inline citation - either a relative path of the form file:docs/research/... or file:mini_ork/... into the worktree, OR the literal GAP for genuinely missing surfaces. The citation sits on the claims[].citations[] array (D1 hard rule C4) and a `miniork_surface` field pointing to the specific file:line anchor in the engine, so a grep on the claim returns both.
yaml_convention: Every claim ends with a `recommended_phase` cell drawn from {P1, P2, P3} (per the F4 phase mapping documented in report-gap-finder.md §2). The F4 'concrete yaml/CLI shape' column is preserved in `proposed_shape`. The miniork_status enum mirrors the source sidecar: present | partial | divergent-by-design | missing | extend | adopt | skip.

claims.semantics_summary: Carry attempt_sha on RunContext plus a per-output <output>.attempt-<sha>.json sidecar so the run can be rewound, diffed across attempts, and inspected by the operator without scraping log files. mini-ork's RunContext (mini_ork/context.py:59) exposes run_id but lacks attempt_sha; the dispatcher writes no per-attempt sidecar. Closing this is a prerequisite for the persistence/time-travel triangle the chapter epic depends on.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Adding attempt_sha + the attempt-<sha> sidecar is the natural extension of any future persistence story; the chapter epic should at least spell out whether the missing surface is a planned gap or a permanent one.
claims.value_any_task: Per-output attempt sha is useful for debuggability; deciding whether to add it costs almost nothing once MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND is on the table.
claims.proposed_shape: Add `attempt_sha` to `RunContext` and write `<output>.attempt-<sha>.json` sidecars from the dispatcher.

claims.semantics_summary: A receipt table keyed by tool name + run_id that records every external side effect after the single-writer lease is acquired, so a crashed run can replay without duplicating an effect. The lease is real (mini_ork/stores/lease.py) and the retry path writes mini_ork/workflow/retry.py artifacts; the effect-boundary half - a <run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json table - is the concrete missing surface. Closing it tightens the chapter's load-bearing durability claim.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Durability is the most-load-bearing chapter claim - the lack of an effect-boundary receipts table is the concrete divergence the chapter must own.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that call external tools use the single-writer lease today; per-tool receipts are the open gap.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce `<run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json` per-tool receipts table keyed by tool name + run_id, integrated with the single-writer lease.

claims.semantics_summary: Consolidate the human-in-the-loop story on a single surface so the chapter claims HITL parity without holding two mirrors. Today the closest analogs are (a) the human_decision_gate edge type declared in schemas/workflow.schema.json §WorkflowEdge.edge_type and (b) the operator-steering channel documented in docs/OPERATOR-STEERING.md; the §14 interrupt + §15 HITL decision is a single source-of-truth question for the chapter epic.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Same direction as §14; the chapter's HITL decision (one surface or two) is the single source of truth.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pause before publish do so today via human_decision_gate.
claims.proposed_shape: Consolidate the HITL decision with §14 - same answer applies.

claims.semantics_summary: A dynamic interrupt(...) call surface so a node can pause the run mid-flight and surface a payload, then resume via Command(resume=...). mini-ork has no in-process interrupt callable; the closed WorkflowNode.type enum has no human_in_the_loop entry, there is no finish_reason: 'interrupt' value, and no <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json payload. The operator-steering channel (docs/OPERATOR-STEERING.md and mini_ork/steering/mid_node_injector.py) is the existing workaround.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Dynamic interrupts are the largest single chapter divergence - the in-process callable has no direct analog - so the chapter epic owns deciding whether to introduce the surface or keep the human_decision_gate + operator-steering workaround.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need mid-run injection use the operator-steering channel today; mid-node inject CLI is the existing workaround.
claims.proposed_shape: Either introduce `type: human_in_the_loop` plus `finish_reason: "interrupt"` plus a <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json payload, or keep the human_decision_gate + operator-steering channel as the documented surface.

claims.semantics_summary: Introduce MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK as a v2 persistence surface, or document the artifact-filesystem + single-writer-lease + recursion-block chain as the permanent answer. The persistence chapter epic is the load-bearing piece of the chapter's parity story; without it the time-travel and fork-shaped CLI decisions (§24) cannot land cleanly.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The chapter epic must decide whether to introduce MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK as a v2 surface or keep documenting divergent-by-design - D1 frames this as the persistence chapter's central question.
claims.value_any_task: Run-level recovery is genuinely needed for long-running recipes; the divergence is real and the chapter owns it.
claims.proposed_shape: Either (a) introduce MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK as a new persistence module, or (b) document the divergence as a permanent reminder that recovery is via the `recursion:` block.

claims.semantics_summary: Promote a five-mode streaming surface (values / updates / events / debug / custom) with a StreamSink class + Stream envelope + a per-channel subscribe CLI. mini-ork's only declared streaming primitive is LiveWriter at mini_ork/dispatch/live_stream.py:80 (append-only with byte cap). The web UI tails LiveWriter via mini_ork/web/routes/node_live.py; recipes that need a typed channel subscribe would need the StreamSink surface.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The five-channel stream surface is one of the chapter's largest divergences (alongside interrupts and persistence); the chapter epic owns whether to introduce a StreamSink class or continue with single-LiveWriter.
claims.value_any_task: The web UI consumes a tail of LiveWriter today; recipes that need a typed channel subscribe would need the StreamSink surface.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce a StreamSink class + Stream envelope + per-channel subscribe CLI (`mini-ork subscribe --run <run_id> --channel events --sink ws://...`) in mini_ork/dispatch/stream.py.

claims.semantics_summary: First-class child-recipe composition so a workflow.yaml can mount a sub-recipe as a node. The recursion: block on the workflow header handles self-recursion but not child-recipe composition; the closed WorkflowNode.type enum has no subrecipe entry and no recipe_ref field. Closing this turns sub-recipe authoring from a copy-paste step into a declarative node.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Sub-recipe composition is the chapter's largest compositional gap; the recursion block on the workflow header handles self-recursion but not child-recipe composition - the chapter epic should frame whether to introduce `type: subrecipe`.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes composed of sub-recipes today route through recursion; once sub-recipe node is a thing, the chapter closes a real workflow authoring pain point.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce `type: subrecipe` plus `recipe_ref: ...` on `WorkflowNode` to enable first-class child-recipe composition.

claims.semantics_summary: Replay a run from a chosen checkpoint by passing run + node + sha; load the persisted state and re-emit events. There is no mini-ork fork CLI today; the per-attempt rewind is the natural follow-on of the persistence chapter epic (§5 + §1) and should not be introduced independently of MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Time travel is the natural follow-on of persistence; the chapter epic should not introduce it independently of §8/§9 - the same MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND decision gates it.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that rewind use the recursion: block today; a per-attempt fork-shaped CLI is the planned gap.
claims.proposed_shape: Tie time travel to the §5 persistence decision - a fork-shaped `mini-ork fork --run --node --sha` CLI plus `<output>.attempt-<sha>.json` sidecars.

claims.semantics_summary: Replace the single global _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 with a named-pool map (per-resource caps, e.g. GPU or rate-limited APIs) and add a per-task SLA field bound to the same pool. mini-ork's whole concurrency story is global today - no per-resource ceiling, no SLA. Closing both is one task and closes a real operational-tooling gap the chapter epic surfaces.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Per-pool concurrency and SLAs are both missing; one task adds both.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes with per-resource concurrency ceilings (e.g., GPU, rate-limited APIs) use pools.
claims.proposed_shape: Replace _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 with a named-pool map and add a per-task SLA field.

claims.semantics_summary: Add a per-asset catalog table that run_summary at mini_ork/cache.py:184 writes into, keyed by (asset_key, partition). Dagster's catalog is the durable surface behind asset-keyed runs; mini-ork has run_summary as a job-level string with no per-asset row. Closing this is a single conditional migration.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A per-asset catalog table is the durable surface behind asset-keyed runs.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that produce tracked assets record catalog rows.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a per-asset catalog table that run_summary at mini_ork/cache.py:184 writes into.

claims.semantics_summary: Add a wait_for_state node type that blocks a run until a named asset state matches, so recipes that depend on upstream freshness can wait cleanly instead of polling. The steering channel (steer_run at mini_ork/web/control.py, guard_steer at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:321) is the closest analog today - a manual nudge, not a sensors primitive. Closing it removes a polling workaround the chapter epic should not carry.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A wait-for-state primitive closes the polling workaround.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that depend on upstream freshness wait cleanly instead of polling.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a 'wait_for_state' node type that blocks until a named asset state matches.

claims.semantics_summary: Document and lock in the two-row pattern (outputs: plus edges: with condition:) as the canonical mini-ork analog of langgraph's Command - an atomic write+pick-next primitive that mini-ork does not introduce. The split is declarative; there is no literal Command return. This is explicitly divergent-by-design and belongs in P3 as chapter-synthesis framing, not as a new surface.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The chapter's stated divergence (no single-return write+pick-next primitive) is honest and the closest analog (outputs: + retries-with-condition:) is well-documented - that's worth preserving in the chapter epic.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need write-and-route atomicity already route through retries-condition pairs; the documented divergence keeps call sites clear.
claims.proposed_shape: Divergent-by-design: keep the two-row pattern (`outputs:` plus `edges:` with `condition:`); no Command analog introduced.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow - XCom-style small-payload inter-task data
claims.semantics_summary: Surface a queryable XCom view on top of run_events so consumers no longer scrape (key, value) rows from mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:165 - tiny decisions, IDs, short summaries stop requiring an artifact round-trip. A small query helper, parameterized by (run_id, key, partition), is the proposed shape.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Surface a queryable XCom view on top of run_events instead of having consumers scrape rows.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pass small values between stages use the XCom view.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an XCom view query helper on top of run_events at mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:165.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow - connections and variables (vault tier)
claims.semantics_summary: Land the vault tier described in config/vault.example.yaml with the env-tier fallback (env -> vault) so secrets stop living as YAML literals. mini_ork/context.py:94 already resolves MINI_ORK_DB / home paths and mini_ork/cli/execute.py reads MINI_ORK_* env vars - the env contract exists today; the secret-store side is missing. The two-tier pattern preserves the simple tier.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Adopt the vault surface via the two-tier pattern (env now, vault later) - see config/vault.example.yaml.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need per-environment secrets use the vault tier; the env tier keeps the simple-tier shape.
claims.proposed_shape: Land the vault tier described in config/vault.example.yaml; document the two-tier fallback (env -> vault).

top_10_backlog.title: Thread / checkpoint id: attempt_sha on RunContext + <output>.attempt-<sha>.json sidecar
top_10_backlog.rationale: Closes the prerequisite half of the persistence/time-travel triangle (langgraph §9); low-cost addition that unblocks §5 and §8 in this list.

top_10_backlog.title: Durable execution: <run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json per-tool receipts table
top_10_backlog.rationale: The effect-boundary half of durability (langgraph §16) - single largest chapter-side surface gap. Keyed by tool name + run_id and integrated with the single-writer lease.

top_10_backlog.title: Human-in-the-loop: consolidate the §14/§15 decision on one surface
top_10_backlog.rationale: Either ship `type: human_in_the_loop` or document human_decision_gate + operator-steering as the answer; the chapter must commit once (§15).

top_10_backlog.title: Interrupts / breakpoints: dynamic in-process interrupt callable
top_10_backlog.rationale: The largest single chapter divergence (§14); land `finish_reason: "interrupt"` + <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json payload, or hold the operator-steering workaround as the documented answer.

top_10_backlog.title: Persistence chapter epic: MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK
top_10_backlog.rationale: Three coupled decisions (§8/§9/§24) gate-reveal one another; ship as one chapter slice or document the dependency explicitly (§5 in this list).

top_10_backlog.title: Streaming: StreamSink class + Stream envelope + per-channel subscribe CLI
top_10_backlog.rationale: Five-mode stream surface divergence (§17); one new module (mini_ork/dispatch/stream.py) plus `mini-ork subscribe --run --channel --sink` Closes a chapter claim.

top_10_backlog.title: Sub-recipe node: type: subrecipe + recipe_ref on WorkflowNode
top_10_backlog.rationale: Closes the recipe-composition gap (§11); without it the chapter cannot claim first-class sub-graph composition.

top_10_backlog.title: Time travel: mini-ork fork --run --node --sha + attempt-<sha> sidecars
top_10_backlog.rationale: Natural follow-on of §5 persistence; tied to the same MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND decision (§24).

top_10_backlog.title: Apache Airflow pools + SLAs: named-pool map and per-task SLA field
top_10_backlog.rationale: Replaces the single _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 with named pools, and adds a per-task SLA field (§3.4). One task, two payoffs.

top_10_backlog.title: Asset-keyed parity: per-asset catalog table behind run_summary
top_10_backlog.rationale: The durable surface behind asset-keyed runs (§4.3); a single conditional migration on mini_ork/cache.py:184.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Persistence chapter epic - three coupled decisions not yet made
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK + attempt_sha + <output>.attempt-<sha>.json sidecar (langgraph §8, §9, §24) are all parallel; resolving one without the others leaves the surface incoherent. The chapter epic should ship them as one chapter slice or document the dependency explicitly.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Operational tooling - scheduler + per-pool concurrency + SLAs
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: mini_ork has no real scheduler (mini_ork/scheduler.py exists but is not wired into the engine entry), no per-pool concurrency (the single _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 is global), and no per-task SLAs. Airflow §3.2 + §3.4 and Temporal §1.5 are all blocked on this; the chapter epic owns wiring mini_ork/scheduler.py + replacing _max_parallel with a named-pool map + adding a per-task SLA field.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Durable execution - journal-driven replay + continue-as-new
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: Temporal §1.1 + §1.6 + Restate §5.4 share the journaled-execution parity axis; the run_events journal written by mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:235 is the source of truth, but classify_outcome at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:216 reads only the last row. The chapter epic owns reading the whole history on resume and adding an in-run continue-as-new analogue bound on history growth.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Streaming chapter epic - StreamSink class or LiveWriter-only
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: LangGraph §17 is the single largest surface divergence after persistence; mini-ork has only LiveWriter at mini_ork/dispatch/live_stream.py and a tail consumer in mini_ork/web/routes/node_live.py. The chapter epic owns deciding whether to ship mini_ork/dispatch/stream.py with a StreamSink class + Stream envelope + `mini-ork subscribe --run --channel --sink` CLI, or keep LiveWriter as the only declared streaming primitive.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Interrupt / HITL chapter epic - single surface or two
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: LangGraph §14 + §15 share the same dynamic-interrupt surface; the chapter epic owns whether to introduce `type: human_in_the_loop` + `finish_reason: "interrupt"` + <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json, or document the human_decision_gate edge + operator-steering channel (docs/OPERATOR-STEERING.md + mini_ork/steering/mid_node_injector.py) as the answer.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Asset-keyed parity - asset-keyed runs + sensors + catalog + lineage
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: The largest structural parity gap. Prefect/Dagster §4.1 + §4.2 + §4.3 + §4.7 form a coupled decision; the chapter epic owns promoting epic_id to a first-class asset key (today opaque to mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:97), adding a 'wait_for_state' node type, surfacing the catalog table behind run_summary, and adding a lineage view alongside _classification_dag.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Saga / compensating handlers - rollback path for fan-out to side effects
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: merge_decisions at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:436 covers forward merge; there is no saga-rollback path. Restate §5.7 is the concrete gap; the chapter epic owns adding a saga-rollback node type that walks back a forward merge_decisions sequence for any recipe that fans out to many side effects.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Resume tokens - checkpoint-token suspend that survives long approvals
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 is cost-only today. Argo §2.4 + Windmill §6.5 share the suspend-with-token gap; the chapter epic owns generalizing pause_cost_run to flow-level suspend that emits a checkpoint resume token the operator or downstream run can re-enter from.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Secrets - vault tier with env-tier fallback
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: Secrets come from the process env today; the env contract at mini_ork/context.py:94 is the only surface. Airflow §3.3 demands a vault tier. The chapter epic owns shipping config/vault.example.yaml with the env-tier fallback so the simple tier stays simple and a per-environment vault can be opted in.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Four-lens chapter synthesis pending
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: The D1 auditor + D1 gap-finder pair sit alongside D2 (stategraph construction), D3 (persistence / checkpointers), and D4 (streaming modes); the chapter synthesis is the public-facing document and is not yet authored. The gap-finder's top_10_backlog and blockers[] arrays are inputs the synthesis must cite 1:1.

hard_rules_preserved: C4 (every claim line has a citation) - preserved by the `citations` field on every claim, each carrying at least one `file:` prefix
F4 (one 8-column row per ranked backlog item) - preserved by the `top_10_backlog` array; every entry carries rank, title, rationale, claims, recommended_phase

F5 (chapter-epic blockers UNRESOLVED by P1, ranked) - preserved by `chapter_epic_remaining_blockers`; every blocker carries id, title, detail, source_lens, source_blocker_id, F5_phase_status; no P1 entries
F1 (breadth-defensible baseline) - preserved; 14 claims covering 9 source-system / lens areas drawn from the two sibling sidecars' D1 coverage maps
F5/Q2 (no invented requirements beyond the sibling sidecars) - every claim's `proposed_shape` mirrors the sibling sidecar's proposed_shape field verbatim
